{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Interface and Support Services Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review findings and negotiation positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. The commercial architecture is materially one-sided in TrueLink's favour on risk allocation: the only liability cap limits TrueLink alone and leaves our liability — including a very broad Client indemnity — entirely uncapped, which is a walk-away position for us. TrueLink's indemnity is narrow (breach/failure to perform only) with no IP infringement, violation of law, unauthorised access, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct triggers, and no indemnity procedure. The Agreement also never confirms that we own Client Content, our borrower/loan data or the Support Services deliverables, even though TrueLink's programmer creates those deliverables for us and TrueLink takes a broad Credit Data licence under § 8(d).

Several operational protections are simply absent: no post-termination data return or transition assistance in a hosting deal where TrueLink holds our data; no performance warranty beyond a Year 2000 warranty; and no insurance requirement at all. On the commercial side, § 3(i) imposes a requirements-style obligation to order every credit report from TrueLink, § 5(a) imposes an open-ended (and still blank) minimum monthly fee, renewal pricing is uncapped after year one, and § 14 is drafted as a service-continuation mechanic rather than a clean convenience right.

Some items are favourable and require no action: no non-compete or field-of-use restraint binds us (§ 2(a) expressly preserves our right to use competing systems), no MFN burdens us (the pricing-parity undertaking runs in our favour), no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by us, and governing law/venue (California; San Luis Obispo County courts, no arbitration) sits within our accepted list.

Two findings did not pass automated verification and are recorded as **needs review** — audit rights and employee non-solicitation. In both cases the deterministic checks failed only because no such clause exists to measure; silence is more favourable to us than our preferred position, and no redline is proposed. Reviewer confirmation is nonetheless recommended.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Issue | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Cap is one-sided (TrueLink only); our liability, including the broad § 12a indemnity, is uncapped. Narrow cap basis, no mutual consequential-damages exclusion, no carve-out set. | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 2 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | § 12.b covers only TrueLink's breach/failure to perform: no IP infringement, violation of law, unauthorised access to Client Content/Credit Data, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; no indemnity procedure. | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 3 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | No Client ownership provision; § 2(d) confirms only TrueLink's rights. Confidentiality treatment under § 10 is not ownership; § 8(d) grants a broad Credit Data licence with no retained-title statement. | Missing | § 2 LICENSE. |
| 4 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | § 3(i) requires us to order the credit report from TrueLink for every borrower underwritten through the Interface, with no category/time limit and no exit for performance failure. | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Grant runs to Client only (no affiliates/contractors); § 13(b) cuts off §§ 2–3 for "any violations or breach" of §§ 8a–8c with no materiality threshold or cure period; no successor transfer. | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. |
| 6 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | § 15 consent regime gives us only a "financially responsible affiliate" carve-out, no successor/M&A carve-out, unqualified consent standard, and no bar on assignment to our competitor. | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 7 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | No liquidated damages or penalties payable by us; § 5(a) amounts are fees for services, and § 14 carries no early-termination fee. | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | No non-compete or field-of-use restraint on us; § 2(a) affirmatively preserves our freedom to acquire, develop or use competing software and services. | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. |
| 9 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | § 9 warrants only Year 2000 date processing: no professional/workmanlike, conformance, compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty, and no repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy. | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT |
| 10 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | No obligation on TrueLink to return our data or assist migration; §§ 13–14 place the burden on us (new name server in 30 days, new hosting in 60 days). | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 11 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | § 5(a) imposes an open-ended (still blank) minimum monthly fee for Hosting and Support Services; § 6 strips our documentation and dispute rights for those minimums. | Deviation | § 5 COMPENSATION. |
| 12 | Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | § 14 is a service-continuation mechanic, cross-references a non-existent "Section 4", allows up to ~60 days to effectiveness, and provides no refund of prepaid fees or bar on minimum-fee charges. | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 13 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Renewal term and 30-day exit window are acceptable, but there is no vendor renewal reminder and no cap on renewal price increases (§ 6 freezes Hosting costs for year one only). | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 14 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | California law (§ 26); exclusive state/federal courts in San Luis Obispo County (§ 27); no arbitration. Within our accepted list. | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | No MFN burdens us; TrueLink undertakes that Hosting Services rates will not exceed those charged to any other party, plus a one-year price freeze. | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. |
| 16 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | No audit, inspection or usage-verification right runs against us; information flows favour us (§ 3(e) usage statistics and logs; § 6 supporting documentation and right to contest). No redline. *Automated check did not verify — reviewer confirmation recommended.* | Needs review | § 2 LICENSE. |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binds us; "employees" appears only in the § 12 indemnities and the § 8(c) access-restriction covenant. No redline. *Automated check did not verify — reviewer confirmation recommended.* | Needs review | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | No insurance provision anywhere, despite TrueLink hosting our Web Site and transmitting Client Content and consumer credit data. | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Uncapped Client liability (LOL-CAP, § 12).** Our playbook treats a cap that protects the vendor alone while leaving our liability — including the very broad § 12a indemnity — uncapped as a walk-away position. We require a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, a mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages, and carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality/data protection and security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, with our payment obligations not treated as capped damages.

*Note on the assignment finding:* although § 15 falls short of our preferred position, there is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right anywhere in the Agreement, so this is a high-severity deviation rather than a walk-away item.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Table the risk-allocation package as a single negotiation.** Present the mutual cap (item 1), the expanded § 12.b indemnity triggers plus a mutual indemnity procedure (item 2), and the Client ownership/assignment-of-deliverables clause with a licence back for embedded TrueLink IP (item 3) together. On the indemnity, the customary-exclusions/remedies package is available as our fallback. We leave the negotiated § 8(d) Credit Data licence intact, clarifying only that it is a licence and not a transfer of ownership.
2. **Press the commercial deviations.** Make credit report ordering optional (fallback: category-limited, 12 months, terminable on service-level failure); delete the § 5(a) minimum monthly fee floor (fallback: floor limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up); extend the licence to affiliates and contractors, add successor transfer and limit the § 13(b) cut-off to uncured material breach; and add the affiliate/successor assignment carve-out, a reasonableness standard on our consent to TrueLink assignments, a no-competitor restriction, and confirmation that our change of control triggers no vendor right.
3. **Close the operational gaps.** Insert into § 14 up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of our data in machine-readable format within thirty days, and deletion with written certification (enforceable post-termination, as §§ 5–30 survive under § 24); add the performance warranty and remedy to § 9; add a 60-day renewal reminder and cap renewal fees at the lesser of CPI and 3% (fallback 5%); conform § 14 to an express convenience right on 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid fees and no penalty; and add the new insurance section (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M).
4. **Resolve open drafting and diligence points.** (a) §§ 5–6 contain unfilled fee blanks and reference Exhibits A and B, which were not in the extracted text — obtain them and re-run the audit rule against them in case they carry a reporting or verification mechanic. (b) The separate "Non-Competition Agreement" referenced at § 8(d) is not defined here and sits outside this document; diligence it separately for any restriction binding us, including any hiring restriction. (c) § 14's cross-reference to "Section 4" does not correspond to any section in the Agreement and should be corrected.
5. **Hold internal discipline on audit.** No audit right currently runs against us and we are not conceding one. If TrueLink later proposes a verification right, hold to once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to our systems."}
